llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions broadly align with a multi-agent dispatcher, but the installation instructions and scripts modify global OpenClaw configuration (openclaw.json), create persistent agent workspaces, set permissive subagent rules, and restart the Gateway — actions that are high‑impact and should be reviewed before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the content: assets, templates, agent roles, DAG templates, and orchestration scripts are present and consistent with a multi-agent dispatcher. However, the skill asks to write global OpenClaw configuration (agents.list / openclaw.json), add six subagents and set main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"], which is powerful — plausible for a dispatcher but worth flagging because it grants broad inter-agent permissions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md mandates running scripts/setup.sh as a required first step and explicitly requires the agent to perform environment detection and install steps before answering user requests. The instructions tell the agent to create/modify ~/.openclaw directories, copy template agent workspaces into ~/.openclaw/agents, write ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, edit openclaw.json (agents.list) and restart the Gateway. These are invasive, persistent system changes and the SKILL.md gives the agent broad discretion during setup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote download/install spec — this is an instruction-only skill with local scripts and assets. That reduces supply-chain risk (no external URL or package fetch documented). Risk remains because scripts are run locally and will write/modify user files, but there is no evidence of arbitrary remote code fetch in the provided manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables or external credentials, yet it modifies global agent configuration and filesystem locations under the user home (~/work, ~/.openclaw/*). It also writes notification configuration that can include Telegram chat IDs (disabled by default). The lack of declared credentials is consistent with the content, but the degree of filesystem/config writes (and the permissive 'allowAgents:["*"]' setting) is disproportionate in the sense of broad privileges vs. a simple helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent files and directories (agent workspaces, sessions, templates, configs), installs a low-frequency watcher, and writes into openclaw.json to add/modify agents and subagent allowances. While always:false and autonomous invocation are normal, modifying global agent list and restarting the Gateway are significant privileges — this skill will persistently alter the agent environment and grant broad subagent permissions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a genuine multi‑agent dispatcher, but it performs high‑impact, persistent changes to your OpenClaw environment. Before installing or running setup.sh: 1) Inspect scripts/setup.sh, scripts/watch.sh, and any script that edits openclaw.json to see exactly what files/keys they change and whether they call external endpoints. 2) Backup your existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and related configs (or test inside a disposable account/container). 3) Pay special attention to the code path that sets main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"] — consider restricting it instead of allowing wildcards. 4) Check for any network/notification code (Telegram/webhooks) and verify chat IDs / endpoints before enabling. 5) If you lack time to audit, run the skill in a sandbox VM/container so its filesystem and gateway restarts cannot affect your primary environment. If you want, provide the full contents of scripts/setup.sh and watch.py and I can point to the exact lines that change configs or perform network actions.
